items.title: Sebi flags risks of relying on GMP as an IPO price guide
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has advised market participants to stop publishing grey market premium figures. These figures may mislead investors regarding potential listing prices of upcoming IPOs. The regulator emphasized that such transactions lack regulatory oversight and settlement guarantees. Furthermore, the grey market does not adhere to any formal price discovery process. The advisory aims to promote transparency and accountability within the securities market.

items.title: Sebi warns of fake WhatsApp, Telegram trading groups
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has issued a critical alert about ongoing scams targeting investors. Fraudsters are utilizing WhatsApp and Telegram to deceive individuals by impersonating official intermediaries while pushing unregulated trading platforms. Investors must remain cautious of invitations to unofficial private groups, as SEBI warns against falling for scams promising improbable returns from global stock markets.

items.title: Tata Steel’s pivot and APL Apollo’s funding burden unsettle investors
items.description: Tata Steel has revealed plans to acquire a significant 26.38% stake in APL Apollo Tubes for an impressive ₹15,510 crore. This strategic move involves Tata Steel transferring its tubes division and Tata Steel Colours to APL Apollo Tubes. However, the announcement triggered a substantial drop in share prices for both companies, raising investor concerns over the potential effects on Tata Steel's operations.

items.title: Sebi moves to prosecute Ketan Parekh
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has initiated prosecution against Ketan Parekh due to allegations of non-compliance in a front-running scheme that reportedly generated illegal profits amounting to ₹66 crore. Despite his request for permission to travel abroad for leisure being denied by the special court, concerns were raised about his prior travel history and required appearances before regulatory authorities.

items.title: Higher interest rates may not hit M&A & IPO growth: Daniel Simkowitz, Morgan Stanley
items.description: Morgan Stanley's Daniel Simkowitz expressed confidence in India's economic growth and potential for mergers and acquisitions. He highlighted opportunities in India's equity and credit markets, particularly in M&A and IPOs. Simkowitz noted that geopolitical volatility affects energy markets, impacting India’s economy. He believes the durability of the M&A market is stronger in India compared to the rest of the world.

items.title: Big 5! ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, RIL, Airtel, SBI drive 45% of Nifty rally
items.description: Between October 8 and November 20, five key bluechip stocks played a pivotal role in enhancing the Nifty's performance, contributing to 45% of its total uptrend. During this time, foreign investors infused approximately $14.33 billion into the Indian market. Analysts emphasize that the current surge in market values is heavily reliant on large-cap stocks, suggesting that broader sector participation is crucial for ongoing market stability and growth.

items.title: Monday Blues! Profit-booking puts brakes on bull run
items.description: On Monday, Indian equities hit a rough patch, resulting in declines for BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty. Investors opted for profit-taking after recent upward trends. The Nifty Bank index took a major hit, dropping over 4%. While US stock futures showed signs of recovery, Asian markets reacted variably following various countries' stabilizing efforts, all amid rising worries about global growth slowdowns and potential US interest rate increases.

items.title: India’s rupee has become an accidental carry star
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India has made moves that temporarily attract carry traders to the rupee. Recent factors include decreasing oil prices and a shift in foreign investment from artificial intelligence stocks to Indian markets. However, these RBI incentives may not last, leaving uncertainty for traders. India's interest rate advantage has significantly diminished since 2011, raising concerns. Policymakers face challenges in ensuring sustained interest in the rupee amid historical depreciation.

items.title: These 8 private and public bank stocks have an upside of up to 29% in one year, according to analysts
items.description: Remember one thing when you look at bank stocks. Their price and the health of the banking system are two different things at this juncture. The system is on a stronger footing than it has been for years, and the Q2 numbers show the clean-up has worked. The stock price swings have to do with the ebb and flow of FPI money, not with the business of the banks themselves.

items.title: PE/VC investments in India surge to USD 8.7 billion in October, highest monthly level in five years: EY-IVCA report
items.description: Private equity and venture capital investments in India surged to USD 8.7 billion in October 2026. This monthly figure is the highest recorded in the past five years, supported by eight large deals totaling USD 7.3 billion. Financial services attracted the majority of investments, amounting to USD 5.9 billion during this period. Despite the increase in investments, exit activity declined, with 21 exits valued at USD 544 million.

items.title: HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries among 10 stocks with highest DII holding in Q2. See full list
items.description: With the rise in the share of MFs and also an overall net investment of Rs 1.69 lakh crore during the quarter, the share of Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) as a whole increased to an all-time high of 19.31% as on September 30, 2026, up from 19.16% as on June 30, 2026. Here are 10 stocks with the highest DII holdings in the September quarter.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A flagship pharma firm for a 4.95% upmove, a mid-cap hospitality stock for a 7% rise
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: A 50 bps jumbo rate hike can lead to financial stability concerns, hurt growth: Report
items.description: SBI economists have lowered their rate hike expectations for the upcoming RBI policy review. They now anticipate a 0.25 per cent increase rather than the previously expected 0.50 per cent. This adjustment stems from concerns regarding financial stability and potential impacts on economic growth. The RBI's monetary policy committee is scheduled to meet from December 2 to December 4.

items.title: Short term is about sentiment, long term about business: 5 smallcap stocks from different sectors with upside potential of up to 30%
items.description: In the market, you cannot wait for all the news to turn good, because by the time it does, stock prices would already have moved up. Also, the market involves risk; it cannot be avoided, only managed. And in the small-cap segment, that means targeting strong businesses run by people who have handled hard times before.

items.title: Investors mint Rs 34.61 lakh cr in November as markets rally nearly 11%
items.description: In a remarkable surge this month, Indian equity markets have observed a substantial upswing, with the BSE Sensex climbing nearly 11 percent. This rally was largely propelled by foreign institutional investors, who contributed record-setting inflows exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore. Motivated by lower crude oil prices and impressive Q2 earnings, investor optimism soared, although a recent profit booking saw a minor dip of nearly 2 percent.

items.title: Nvidia share price could double as Jensen Huang returns as CEO, says deVere Group’s Nigel Green. Here’s why
items.description: Nvidia could double its market value following Jensen Huang’s return as CEO, potentially pushing the AI giant to fresh highs and lifting global markets, according to deVere Group CEO Nigel Green. Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% intraday on Monday before closing 32% higher.

items.title: The LTCG debate: Why markets need tax stability and not ad-hoc fixes
items.description: Foreign Institutional Investor capital is leaving Indian markets, raising concerns over the unpredictability of tax policies. Investors are urging for the reconsideration of Long-Term Capital Gains tax provisions. Historical changes in LTCG have created volatility that affects long-term investors negatively. A stable tax policy framework is essential to attract and retain investment in the Indian financial market.
